neighbours.label: ' know' when the knowing is lacking or falls short: under negation (does not know how, don't know where) or in 'should know better'. The - pole takes the other side, affirmed knowledge (I know, she knew of)
fire: Most first-year students do not know how to cite a source properly.
A grown man in his position really should know better.
The new puppy does not know yet where it is allowed to sleep.
Many voters didn't know what the measure would actually change.
People who have never sailed do not know how quickly the weather turns.
At her age she ought to know better than to trust such a promise.
Small children do not know when to stop eating sweets.
The interns did not know whom to ask for help.
quiet: Most first-year students know how to find a book in the library.
A grown man in his position surely knows the rules.
The old dog knows exactly where it is allowed to sleep.
Many voters know what the measure would actually change.
People who have sailed for years know how quickly the weather turns.
At her age she can tell at once whether to trust such a promise.
Small children do not like to stop eating sweets.
The interns did not ask anyone for help.

notes: Card: + pole ' know' x21, ' better' x4 in 'does not know yet how', 'should know better', 'didn't know how', 'don't know where'; - pole ' know'/' knows' in affirmative 'I know', 'she knew of', 'he knows that'. Probes: 'does not know how' 0.51, 'should know better' 0.72, 'don't know where' 0.22; 'I know this town' 0.04, 'She knew of' 0.04, 'They know how to' 0.13.
